title: A walk without the tab bar
question: While you're walking, the tab bar stays on screen. A walk should be a focused screen with a clear way back. Which way for this and any other full-screen task on the phone? I've built A; B stays here if you'd rather it.

options.label: A: The tab bar steps aside; ‹ Outreach stays (built)
options.thesis: The tab bar steps aside while the walk is open, as it does for the keyboard. The way out is the same ‹ Outreach and swipe back as every pushed page; the walk keeps going and Outreach shows it as Your walk.
options.viewport: Walking on a 390 phone: masthead with the street, the map, progress, two mark buttons and Pause · ⋯ · Finish at the foot, nothing under it.
options.risk: A swipe from the edge leaves the walk screen (the walk itself carries on).

options.label: B: Full screen with Close
options.thesis: The walk opens like a full-screen sheet: a round ✕ at the top right closes it, no Back and no swipe back.
materials: a close button on the masthead
options.viewport: The same walking screen with ✕ at the top right instead of ‹ Outreach.
options.risk: A second way of leaving a page that only this screen has; ✕ can read as ending the walk.

options.label: Today: the tab bar stays
options.thesis: What it does now, for comparison.
options.viewport: The walking screen above the tab bar.
options.risk: A tap on a tab leaves the walk mid-street; less room for the map.
